draft.description: Signed major-radius separation, in m, between a measurement position mapped along its magnetic flux surface to the outboard midplane and the separatrix there: ΔR = R_mapped − R_sep,mid. The mapping preserves the magnetic flux label. The outboard midplane is the low-field-side point of maximum major radius on the relevant flux surface, with R greater than the magnetic-axis major radius. Here R is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. The separation is positive outside the separatrix on the scrape-off-layer side, zero on the separatrix, and negative on the confined-plasma side.
draft.documentation: This scalar expresses a measurement position's separation from the separatrix after flux-surface mapping to the outboard midplane. It is obtained by subtracting the major radius of the outboard-midplane separatrix intersection from the major radius of the mapped measurement position. It is a dimensional difference of major radii, not a normalized flux coordinate, a radial coordinate assigned to a flux surface, an unmapped local separation, or the shortest distance normal to the separatrix. The same quantity applies to embedded and reciprocating Langmuir-probe measurements and Thomson-scattering channels.
draft.name: radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_midplane

draft.description: Azimuthal angular coordinate of a point on a control surface about the machine symmetry axis, expressed in rad in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. It is defined by phi = atan2(y, x) modulo 2*pi, with zero at the facility-defined reference direction and positive angle counterclockwise when viewed from +Z toward the origin. The source supplies an array of these angles on which the Fourier decomposition of the normal magnetic-field component is carried out.
draft.documentation: This quantity locates control-surface points toroidally, rather than locating a launching position, diagnostic measurement position, aperture or antenna strap. It is an angular coordinate, not an angular offset from another position, a radial or vertical coordinate of the control surface, or a magnetic-field component evaluated there. Each array entry is a scalar angle; angles differing by an integer multiple of 2*pi describe the same toroidal direction. The array provides the toroidal sampling locations for the control-surface Fourier decomposition.
draft.name: toroidal_angle_of_control_surface

draft.description: Toroidal electromotive force at the plasma boundary, defined as the last closed magnetic flux surface bounding the confined plasma. It is obtained from the electric-field circulation V_loop = ∮_C E·dl around a closed toroidal loop C on that surface and is expressed in V. Positive voltage drives positive ohmic plasma current, flowing anticlockwise when viewed from above, along increasing toroidal angle in a right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It includes inductive contributions from both external sources and plasma currents, rather than only the externally generated contribution.
draft.documentation: This scalar describes the inductive voltage driving ohmic current at the last closed magnetic flux surface, where the poloidal magnetic flux equals its boundary value. Unlike average_external_loop_voltage, which is obtained from the negative time derivative of the prescribed average externally applied poloidal magnetic flux, this quantity is the total boundary loop voltage. It is an electromotive force around a closed toroidal path, not an electrostatic potential difference between two points, and is distinct from current_due_to_ohmic_current_drive, the resulting resistively driven current measured in amperes.
draft.name: loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary

draft.description: Signed magnetic flux through the surface bounded by the contour formed by intersecting the magnetic flux surface through the evaluation point with a plane of constant vertical coordinate Z. For an axisymmetric configuration, this is the horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis, and the full flux is ψ(R,Z) = 2π ∫₀ᴿ B_Z(R′,Z) R′ dR′, where R is major radius and B_Z is the vertical magnetic-field component. The surface normal points toward increasing Z, so upward net field gives positive flux. The quantity is expressed in Wb, without division by 2π, normalization, or spatial averaging.
draft.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux is a scalar function whose level sets label magnetic surfaces in axisymmetric equilibrium. It includes the magnetic field from both plasma currents and external sources, unlike external magnetic flux, which excludes the plasma-generated contribution. It differs from toroidal magnetic flux, which integrates the toroidal magnetic field through a poloidal cross-section, and from the dimensionless normalized poloidal flux coordinate. This record describes the flux function generally, rather than its evaluation at a designated magnetic axis, plasma boundary, diagnostic position, or individual flux loop; such quantities are location- or object-specific specializations.
draft.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux

draft.description: Total power deposited on a single divertor target by recombination at the plasma-material interface, obtained by adding the plasma-ion and neutral-particle recombination contributions. It is inferred from edge-plasma simulations or from particle-flux measurements combined with surface energy-release models. The deposited power is non-negative and is expressed in W.
draft.documentation: This quantity combines the contributions represented separately by plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination and neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination. It describes recombination energy deposited at one divertor target, rather than recombination power summed over all targets in the divertor assembly. Its target-specific scope also distinguishes it from recombination power at wall surfaces generally and from power_due_to_recombination, which has no restriction to a particular surface location.
draft.name: power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination

draft.description: Signed toroidal orientation angle of a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil’s sensitive-axis normal, expressed in rad. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, it is obtained as α_tor = atan2(n_φ, n_R), where n_R and n_φ are the radial and toroidal components of the sensitive-axis unit normal. The angle is measured from +R toward the normal’s horizontal projection and is positive toward increasing φ; zero corresponds to a normal in the poloidal plane with its horizontal projection along +R.
draft.documentation: This scalar describes the orientation of an individual poloidal magnetic-field probe coil, not the probe’s toroidal position or a component of the measured magnetic field. Its horizontal projection specifies the toroidal orientation of the sensitive direction used to project the local magnetic field onto the probe response. It differs from the toroidal angle of a toroidal magnetic-field probe by the sensor type, and from a poloidal orientation angle by the plane in which the orientation is measured. It is not averaged over probes, turns, or field samples.
draft.name: toroidal_angle_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe

draft.description: Radial derivative dV/dρ_tor of the cumulative volume V enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface with respect to its dimensionful toroidal-flux coordinate ρ_tor, measured in metres, with time and other independent coordinates held fixed. The derivative has unit m^2.
draft.documentation: This geometric quantity is obtained by differentiating the volume enclosed by each nested magnetic flux surface with respect to the dimensionful toroidal-flux coordinate: D_V = dV/dρ_tor. The volume is accumulated over the full interior from the magnetic axis to the selected surface, rather than being the volume of a shell. Thus a small coordinate increment corresponds to an enclosed-volume increment dV = D_V dρ_tor. For an outward-increasing coordinate, the enclosed volume increases outward and the derivative is nonnegative. This quantity is distinct from the enclosed volume itself, its derivative with respect to poloidal magnetic flux, the analogous derivative of poloidal cross-sectional area, and the temporal derivative of D_V. It is a geometric quantity without species weighting.
draft.name: derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate

draft.description: Plasma current (Ip) is the net signed toroidal conventional electric current, in A, flowing through the plasma column. It is the integral of toroidal plasma current density over the full poloidal plasma cross-section, with opposing contributions combined algebraically. Positive current is anticlockwise when viewed from above. Values may be obtained from magnetic measurements or calculated from a reconstructed MHD equilibrium; the fibre-optic current sensor (FOCS) reports the total toroidal current through the area outlined by its fibre path, measured through the Faraday magneto-optic effect.
draft.documentation: This quantity describes the total toroidal plasma current rather than a current density, a runaway-electron contribution, a field-aligned current, or the current enclosed by an interior magnetic flux surface. It is also distinct from current assigned to an individual plasma filament, delivered to a divertor target, or carried by a coil or passive structure. Measured and equilibrium-reconstructed values represent the same physical quantity, not separate current components. Magnetic estimates can use several calculation methods, with the generally recommended method listed first. For a FOCS estimate, the stated integration region is the area enclosed by the sensor path; its interpretation must retain that measurement boundary.
draft.name: plasma_current

draft.description: Full non-negative clear-aperture extent of an optical element along X2, its second object-local tangential axis, for rectangular aperture geometry (geometry_type = 3). It is obtained as w = X2,max - X2,min, the difference between opposing aperture-edge coordinates along X2, and is expressed in m.
draft.documentation: This scalar describes the full width of the optical element's usable rectangular opening, not its half-width or the external extent of its mount. The coordinates X1 and X2 lie in the object-local aperture plane. The X2 direction distinguishes this quantity from the first local tangential width, which is measured along X1; unlike a second local tangential coordinate, it measures an edge-to-edge extent rather than a signed position relative to the local origin. It applies only when geometry_type = 3.
draft.name: second_local_tangential_width_of_optical_element

draft.description: Net conventional electric current incident on one complete divertor, obtained by integrating the charged-particle current density over the union of all its target surfaces, with electron and ion contributions combined using their signed charges. The current is positive for conventional current flowing from the plasma into the material and is expressed in A. It excludes neutral-particle flux and displacement current.
draft.documentation: The divertor is treated as a complete physical assembly, rather than a single target or tile. Its current is I = ∫S Σs qs Γs · n dA, where S comprises all target surfaces of this divertor, qs is the signed charge of species s, Γs is its particle flux density, and n points from the plasma toward the material. This assembly-integrated current differs from current_at_divertor_target, which applies to one target, and current_of_divertor_tile, which applies to one individual tile; it does not sum over separate divertor assemblies.
draft.name: current_of_divertor

draft.documentation: The quantity is identical to the existing ethylene_equivalent_electron_source_rate: instantaneous ethylene injection into the plasma vessel, counted as 16 equivalent electrons per molecule. No physical distinction is supplied that would support a separate record; the equivalent-electron counting convention alone does not justify a different name.

draft.description: Calibrated, wavelength-resolved photon arrival rate from plasma radiation along a specified viewing direction, per projected collecting area, viewing solid angle, and wavelength interval. It is defined by dN_gamma = L_gamma(lambda) dt dA_perp dOmega dlambda, where A_perp is the collecting area projected perpendicular to the ray direction. The spectral density is per unit wavelength, not per frequency or photon energy, and its unit is m^-3.s^-1.sr^-1.
draft.documentation: Spectral photon radiance expresses the absolute photon-number brightness measured by a spectrometer channel along its viewing direction. It includes the line and continuum contributions at the specified wavelength without restriction to an emitting species or mechanism; spectral bremsstrahlung photon radiance instead selects only free-free emission. Unlike photon radiance at a spectral line, this quantity remains wavelength-resolved rather than being background-subtracted and integrated over an identified line. It is neither an energy radiance nor a local volumetric photon-production rate, and its calibrated photon scale distinguishes it from an uncalibrated detector count rate.
draft.name: spectral_photon_radiance

draft.description: Real part of the radial component of the perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction in the vacuum region outside the plasma, obtained from linear MHD stability analysis for a given toroidal mode number. It is Re(A_vac · e_R), where A_vac is the complex perturbation eigenfunction and e_R points toward increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. The real part is taken relative to the eigenfunction's phase reference, and positive values indicate an outward real radial projection. The unit is T.m.
draft.documentation: This quantity describes one toroidal mode of the vacuum magnetic vector-potential perturbation, not a sum over modes. It retains only the real radial component, rather than the imaginary component or the full complex radial component. The radial direction is away from the toroidal symmetry axis, distinguishing it from poloidal and toroidal components. The vacuum locus distinguishes it from plasma-region vector-potential perturbations, and the vector potential, measured in T.m, is distinct from the corresponding magnetic-field perturbation, measured in T. Its physics context is linear magnetohydrodynamic stability rather than gyrokinetics.
draft.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part

draft.description: Dimensionless plasma-pressure beta relative to a current-based poloidal magnetic-pressure scale, defined as beta_p = 4 integral_V(p dV)/(R_0 mu_0 I_p^2), with unit 1. Here p is the supplied plasma pressure, V is the evaluation volume, R_0 is the reference major radius, mu_0 is vacuum permeability, and I_p is the plasma current used in the normalization. It uses a poloidal rather than a toroidal magnetic-pressure reference.
draft.documentation:
Poloidal beta measures plasma pressure loading relative to an effective poloidal magnetic-pressure scale. Writing the volume-averaged pressure as

_V = integral_V(p dV)/V, the source normalization is equivalent to beta_p = 2 mu_0

_V/B_p,ref^2 with B_p,ref^2 = mu_0^2 I_p^2 R_0/(2V); this reference field is a current-based scale, not a pointwise poloidal field. Global values use the plasma volume, while the radial profile evaluates pressure content inside the corresponding flux surface. For the equilibrium-reconstructed estimate, p is the pressure determined by the reconstruction code. Unlike toroidal beta, this quantity uses the poloidal reference; unlike pedestal electron beta, it is not defined from local electron pressure at a specified pedestal position. It is neither an unnormalized pressure nor an average of local pressure-to-field ratios, and its normalization requires nonzero plasma current.
draft.name: poloidal_beta

draft.description: Mean perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis over a complete closed magnetic flux surface, obtained as ⟨R⟩ψ = (∮ R dS/|∇ψ|)/(∮ dS/|∇ψ|), where R is the pointwise major radius, dS is the surface-area element, and ψ is the poloidal magnetic flux labeling the surface. This normalized average is weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient. Its unit is m.
draft.documentation: This scalar geometric equilibrium coefficient is specified on each closed magnetic flux surface as a function of poloidal magnetic flux, wherever the defining average is well defined and finite. It is the flux-surface average of major radius, not a volume average or the major-radius coordinate at a selected point such as the inboard midplane. Unlike the related averages of inverse major radius and inverse squared major radius, it averages R itself; in particular, its reciprocal generally differs from the flux-surface average of 1/R.
draft.name: flux_surface_averaged_major_radius

draft.description: Signed toroidal component of the total conventional electric current density, provided as one scalar value per element in the specified grid subset. It is obtained as j_phi = e_phi · j_tot = sum_k(e_phi · j_k), an algebraic sum of all included current-density contributions, not a sum of their magnitudes. The unit vector e_phi points toward increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, so positive values indicate conventional charge transport in that direction. The unit is A.m^-2.
draft.documentation: This quantity fixes the signed projection of total current density to the toroidal direction, rather than the radial or poloidal direction. It represents the total of the included contributions, not a current selected by particle species, orbit class, or generation mechanism. The sources provide one scalar per grid-subset element for edge-plasma, plasma, or wall-physics quantities; the name therefore imposes no plasma-only or wall-only locus. It is a current-density component, not a vector magnitude, a flux-surface-averaged current density, or a spatially integrated current.
draft.name: toroidal_total_current_density

draft.description: Non-inductive auxiliary power coupled to the whole plasma, obtained by summing the coupled power from all neutral-beam injection, electron-cyclotron, ion-cyclotron and lower-hybrid systems, excluding Ohmic power. It includes auxiliary input used for heating and non-inductive current drive, rather than only energy deposited as thermal heating. Expressed in W.
draft.documentation: This quantity is the aggregate external auxiliary power input, P_ext = sum_s P_s, where P_s is the power coupled to the plasma by each included auxiliary source. It is not resolved by source, plasma species or spatial region. Unlike general plasma heating power, it excludes Ohmic heating and internally generated fusion heating and can include power contributing to non-inductive current drive. Unlike source-specific heating powers, it combines all included auxiliary systems; unlike generator or launched power, it counts only power coupled to the plasma.
draft.name: external_heating_power

draft.description: Complex scalar E-minus (E−) component of the coherent wave electric field perpendicular to the static magnetic field, designated right-hand circularly polarized by the source. It is obtained from a full-wave-code solution for a specified wave frequency and time slice, with one scalar value per element of a grid subset, in V.m^-1.
draft.documentation: This quantity is the scalar circular-polarization component E−, not a vector contribution to the electric field. The source identifies it as the right-hand component of the perpendicular wave electric field and states that it drives ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH). It is distinct from the complementary left-hand E-plus component, the parallel wave electric field, and the complete wave-electric-field vector. It retains the complex component rather than only its amplitude or imaginary quadrature. Values are provided on subsets of a generic grid, without restriction to a beam or ray path. The source does not specify a circular-basis normalization or temporal phasor convention, so no particular formula or sense of rotation relative to ion gyromotion is imposed here.
draft.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field

draft.description: Dimensionless orientation indicator for the equilibrium toroidal magnetic-field component at a flux surface in local gyrokinetic geometry. For nonzero B_phi, it is obtained as s_phi = sgn(B_phi) = B_phi/|B_phi|, where B_phi = B · e_phi and e_phi points toward increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. It equals +1 along increasing phi and -1 in the opposite direction, and is undefined when B_phi is zero. Unit: 1.
draft.documentation: This scalar specifies the orientation, not the strength, of the toroidal magnetic field at the flux surface. It specializes the generic magnetic-field orientation indicator by selecting the toroidal component and the flux-surface locus. Unlike the toroidal magnetic field itself, it retains only the sign and carries no field magnitude. It does not indicate plasma-current direction or the even or odd reflection symmetry of a gyrokinetic eigenmode.
draft.name: parity_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_at_flux_surface

draft.description: Flux-surface-averaged rate of collisional energy transfer per unit volume to the co-passing part of a fast-particle distribution from one specified ion species and charge state, in W.m^-3. The profile is evaluated using the co-passing part of the distribution. Positive values denote energy gain by that fast-particle population; negative values denote energy loss to the specified ion charge state.
draft.documentation: This quantity resolves the collisional power received by co-passing fast particles through exchange with a specified ion charge state. The co-passing restriction applies to the fast-particle distribution receiving the power, not to the background ion charge state. The source does not identify that background charge state as a fast-ion population. Unlike total co-passing fast-particle collisional power density, this quantity includes only the exchange with the specified ion species and charge state, with no sum over charge states or collision partners. It excludes counter-passing and trapped contributions and is distinct from power transferred from fast particles to thermal ions. Both bound profile structures describe flux-surface-averaged evaluation; the quantity is a power per volume, not stored energy density or volume-integrated power.
draft.name: co_passing_fast_power_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_ion_state

draft.documentation: The identifying name collides with the existing weight_of_interferometer_beam record, which already describes the factor assigned to one beam’s line-integrated electron-density residual in a weighted objective. No distinct quantity is established by the supplied family or source. Equilibrium reconstruction supplies the objective’s context rather than a distinguishing physical quantity. The source specifies a dimensionless weight w_i entering as J = (1/2) sum_i w_i^2 [(reconstructed_i - measured_i)/sigma_i]^2, where sigma_i is the measurement-error standard deviation; this convention belongs in the existing record’s definition.
draft.name: weight_of_interferometer_beam

draft.description: The electromotive-force contribution to the plasma loop voltage from time-varying externally generated poloidal magnetic flux, including contributions from active coils and magnetically coupled passive conducting structures. It is obtained as V_ext(t) = -dPhi_ext(t)/dt, where Phi_ext is the external poloidal magnetic flux linked by the considered closed toroidal plasma circuit. The unit is V. Positive voltage denotes an induced electromotive force with positive line integral in the direction of increasing toroidal angle phi in a right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame.
draft.documentation: This scalar describes the externally generated inductive contribution, rather than the total loop voltage at the plasma boundary. It includes the linked-flux response of passive conducting structures as well as active coil circuits, but excludes resistive voltage drops and non-inductive contributions. Unlike average_external_loop_voltage, which is obtained from the prescribed average poloidal flux applied by external poloidal-field coils, this quantity is defined from the external flux linked by the considered toroidal plasma circuit; no averaging prescription is specified.
draft.name: external_loop_voltage

draft.description: Radial shift of the final deposition location of ablated pellet material relative to its ablation location attributable to E×B drift. It is obtained as the normalized toroidal flux coordinate at final deposition minus that at ablation, Δρ_tor,N = ρ_tor,N,dep − ρ_tor,N,abl, and is dimensionless (unit 1).
draft.documentation: Each value describes the deposition shift of material ablated at the corresponding point along the pellet path, rather than a path-integrated displacement. The normalized toroidal flux coordinate measures radial position across flux surfaces; its difference is not a displacement in the toroidal direction or a geometric distance. The quantity includes only redistribution attributed to E×B drift and is distinct from an absolute deposition coordinate, a drift velocity, the pellet's injection motion, and cumulative distance along the pellet path.
draft.name: radial_displacement_of_pellet_deposition_due_to_e_cross_b_drift

draft.description: Signed effective number of turns assigned to one cross-section element of a passive axisymmetric conducting loop for calculating the loop's magnetic field. It weights the element's current contribution in the magnetic-field calculation; a positive value means that current is counter-clockwise when seen from above. The quantity is dimensionless, with unit 1.
draft.documentation: Each passive loop comprises individually described cross-section elements, and this quantity applies to one such element, not to an aggregate over the loop or over multiple loops. It specifies the effective winding contribution and its orientation rather than the current itself or the element's conducting cross-sectional area. Its passive-loop-element locus distinguishes it from the effective turn count of a coil conductor element and from turn counts assigned to correction coils, toroidal-field coils, or magnetic probes.
draft.name: turn_count_of_passive_loop_element

draft.description: Non-negative geometric separation between the two bounding interfaces of a single layer within a breeder blanket module, evaluated at the midplane and expressed in m.
draft.documentation: This scalar describes the through-material thickness of one breeder blanket layer at the midplane, rather than an unspecified local thickness elsewhere in the layer. It applies to an individual layer, not to the total blanket-module build or the module's upper or lower cap thickness. It is distinct from the layer's width, height, volume, composition fractions and nuclear heating quantities. The source specifies the midplane evaluation locus but does not prescribe a measurement method or thickness direction.
draft.name: thickness_of_breeder_blanket_layer_at_midplane

draft.description: Characteristic time, in s, for the decrease of electric-current magnitude during a disruption, applying to total plasma current or current carried by a specified particle population. Under a linear-threshold convention, the extrapolated full-decay time is [t(f_low) - t(f_high)]/(f_high - f_low), where the fractions refer to a specified reference current magnitude and t(f) is the time at which the decaying magnitude reaches fraction f. Under an exponential convention, it is the e-folding time tau in I(t) = I_0 exp[-(t - t_0)/tau]. The selected current, reference magnitude and decay convention must be specified.
draft.documentation: This scalar describes disruption-driven electric-current decay without restricting the current to a particular population or imposing one decay convention. The plasma-current specialization uses the linear 20–80% construction, [t(0.2) - t(0.8)]/0.6; the runaway-electron specialization describes total toroidal runaway-electron current and permits custom linear, fixed 20–80% linear or exponential conventions. These population-specific times need not agree, and a linear-extrapolated time is not generally equal to an exponential e-folding time. This quantity does not describe local current-density decay or electron-temperature decay, whether volume-averaged or evaluated at the magnetic axis.
draft.name: decay_time_due_to_disruption

draft.description: Local number density of hydrogen ions (H+) in the scrape-off-layer plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter, expressed in m^-3. It counts hydrogen ions per unit physical volume, excluding neutral hydrogen, deuterium, tritium and other ion species. The precise plasma evaluation point relative to the sheath or magnetic presheath is not specified.
draft.documentation: This quantity is the hydrogen-specific component of density_at_limiter in the species-resolved ion-density summary. It describes the local hydrogen-ion population rather than electrons or other ion species; the positive-charge-state sum for hydrogen contains only H+. The limiter locus distinguishes it from hydrogen density at the last closed flux surface or at a divertor target. The source supplies a density value at the limiter location but specifies neither a measurement or calculation method nor a precise sheath-relative evaluation point.
draft.name: hydrogen_density_at_limiter

draft.description: Measured angular phase of a probing wave beam, expressed in rad. For the reflectometer it is measured for each probing frequency and sweep-begin time relative to the phase at launch. For the refractometer it is the phase of the probing-signal envelope, also relative to launch, rather than the carrier oscillation phase. A launch-referenced value is obtained as the measured phase minus the launch phase using the same phase convention. For the interferometer it is the phase measured at the specified wavelength after correction for fringe jumps. The sources do not specify a common phasor-sign convention or phase-branch interval.
draft.documentation: This quantity describes the phase of a diagnostic probing beam, not the phase of an antenna strap current or antenna excitation, the beam's reference frequency, or its wavefront curvature. Launch referencing, envelope interpretation and fringe-jump correction are specified according to the diagnostic source rather than added to the name. Phase values separated by an integer multiple of 2π rad are equivalent modulo a full revolution; an unwrapped representation can retain accumulated revolutions. The interferometer source requires fringe-jump correction but does not specify its algorithm, and the launch-referenced sources do not prescribe a wrapping interval or sign convention.
draft.name: wave_phase_of_wave_beam

draft.description: Lower photon-energy boundary of an X-ray detection or emission energy band, expressed in eV. For a detector-pixel counting threshold, it is the assigned value E_gamma,min that an incident photon must exceed to be eligible for counting: E_gamma > E_gamma,min. For channel energy bands or an emissivity profile, it specifies the band's low-energy boundary; the emissivity-profile band is assumed common to all channels used in reconstruction.
draft.documentation: Together with upper_photon_energy, this quantity defines an X-ray spectral window. A pixel counting threshold applies individually to the specified pixel, not as a detector-wide average. The quantity describes a lower band boundary rather than the upper boundary, a representative pixel photon energy, or photon-energy coordinates used for response calibration. It is not restricted to the spectral bandpass of a crystal-spectrometer pixel. Exceeding a counting threshold is necessary for registration but does not imply unit detection efficiency; detection efficiency is a separate quantity.
draft.name: lower_bound_photon_energy

draft.documentation: The source specifies a processed infrared image in apparent temperature, in K, rather than the thermodynamic temperature of the surface material. This distinction must be retained in the name, but the supplied closed qualifier vocabulary does not include apparent. The image contains pixel-level values, distinct from maximum_surface_temperature; the source does not specify the radiance-to-temperature conversion convention.

draft.description: Major-radius coordinate R of a specified reference point in a poloidal-field coil's cross-sectional geometry, equal to its nonnegative perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, in m. It is given by R = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), where x and y are the transverse coordinates in a right-handed Cartesian frame whose z axis coincides with the toroidal symmetry axis. The reference point is the annulus center or the first or second endpoint of the central segment defining a thick-line element, as specified by the geometry.
draft.documentation: This scalar locates a reference point in the cross-sectional geometry of an active poloidal-field coil, including central-solenoid and shaping coils. For an annular element it locates the annulus center; for a thick-line element it locates one endpoint of the central segment used with a perpendicular thickness to define the rectangular approximation. It is not necessarily the coordinate of the coil center and is not an average over the coil. Unlike the radial outline of a poloidal-field coil, it does not describe the complete cross-sectional boundary; unlike the inner and outer radii of an annular coil element, it is measured from the toroidal symmetry axis rather than from the annulus center.
draft.name: radial_coordinate_of_poloidal_field_coil

draft.description: Absolute thermodynamic temperature of a selected sensor at its thermocouple junction, measured by the thermocouple and expressed in K. It describes the local thermal state at that individual sensor, not an average or other aggregate over the sensor set.
draft.documentation: This scalar quantity characterizes the local thermal condition at a selected thermocouple sensor attached to a tokamak structural component. The enclosing set of sensors supplies collection context only; each value belongs to one sensor member. The locus is the sensor junction, rather than coolant at an inlet, outlet, or plant-component port, and the quantity is not a temperature assigned to an entire coil conductor or neutron detector assembly. It describes thermal state, in contrast to acceleration or displacement measured at a structural sensor location.
draft.name: temperature_of_sensor

draft.description: The smallest pressure-volume gas throughput that a gas injection valve can reliably deliver, defining the lower operational bound of its controllable range. Gas throughput is Q_g = p_g dV_g/dt, where p_g is the gas pressure at the flow boundary and dV_g/dt is the volumetric flow rate across that boundary. The lower-bound throughput is expressed in Pa.m^3.s^-1.
draft.documentation: This quantity specifies the lower reliable operating limit of a gas injection valve connecting a gas bottle to pipes. It describes the aggregate gas stream, not a selected molecular species, mass flow, or particle-number rate. Unlike gas_flow or gas_flow_of_valve, it is an operating limit rather than an unrestricted delivered throughput; unlike maximum_gas_flow, it marks the lower rather than the upper end of the valve's controllable range.
draft.name: lower_bound_gas_flow

draft.description: Dimensionless collisionality for a specified pair of particle species, obtained by dividing their collision frequency by a characteristic transit frequency: nu_ab_star = nu_ab / f_transit. Both frequencies have reciprocal-time units, giving unit 1.
draft.documentation: This quantity measures collisional relaxation between two particle species relative to characteristic transit motion in the local gyrokinetic collision model. It is specified for a species pair rather than for electrons alone, and it is not restricted to the pedestal top. Its transit-frequency normalization distinguishes it from the neighbouring electron collisionalities normalized by a trapped-electron bounce frequency; it is also distinct from the dimensional collision frequency itself.
draft.name: collisionality_between_species

draft.documentation: No source text is bound to this target. The incumbent describes the local curvature radius of a circular arc on a coil cross-sectional contour, whereas its name identifies a coil radius. Without a bound source, the intended locus and its distinction from radius_of_coil_conductor_element cannot be established reliably.

draft.description: Incident angle of the local magnetic field with respect to the plasma-facing component surface at the Langmuir-probe location, expressed in rad. The source does not specify a calculation method, sign convention or angular range.
draft.documentation: This scalar describes magnetic-field incidence on the plasma-facing component surface at an embedded or reciprocating Langmuir probe, supporting interpretation of ion saturation current measurements. It is not the mechanical tilt of the probe or the orientation of its collector surface. Unlike the effective collection area of a Langmuir probe, it is an angle rather than a projected area.
draft.name: surface_incident_angle_of_magnetic_field_at_langmuir_probe

draft.description: Fourier coefficient of the component of the non-axisymmetric vacuum error magnetic field normal to a specified control surface, obtained by Fourier decomposition of that normal component over the surface points. The coefficient has unit T.
draft.documentation: This quantity represents the normal vacuum error field on a control surface in Fourier-coefficient form, rather than as the local normal field values or the full magnetic-field vector. The normal direction is that of the control surface; the source does not establish that the control surface is a magnetic flux surface. It does not specify the Fourier basis, phase convention, coefficient normalization, or orientation of the surface normal.
draft.name: normal_non_axisymmetric_vacuum_magnetic_field_fourier_coefficient_at_control_surface

draft.description: Dimensionless scalar ratio T_p/T_ref, obtained by dividing the kinetic temperature T_p of a selected particle species by the positive reference temperature T_ref on the same magnetic flux surface. The numerator and denominator use the same temperature unit, giving the ratio unit 1.
draft.documentation: This quantity gives the temperature of a selected species, including electrons, relative to the reference thermal scale used in a local gyrokinetic flux-tube simulation. It retains the species dependence of the numerator and depends on the specified reference temperature. Unlike an absolute particle temperature, it is dimensionless; unlike magnetic-axis-to-volume-averaged electron or ion temperature ratios, it compares a species temperature with a reference scale rather than measuring temperature-profile peaking.
draft.name: ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_particle_reference_temperature

draft.description: Dimensionless squareness coefficient of the lower-inner (below-center, inboard or high-field-side) quadrant of a nested magnetic flux surface, defined using the convention of T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009. It measures signed departure from a reference ellipse with the same center, horizontal half-width, and elongation: zero denotes no additional corner shaping, positive values denote boxier corners, and negative values denote more indented or diamond-like corners. It is a quadrant-specific coefficient, not an average of upper and lower inner squareness, and has unit 1.
draft.documentation: This quantity is provided on the equilibrium's one-dimensional radial grid as a function of poloidal magnetic flux, with each value describing a surface of constant magnetic-flux label. The reference ellipse in a right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame is parameterized by R = R0 + a cos θ and Z = Z0 + κa sin θ, where (R0, Z0) is its center, a its horizontal half-width, and κ its elongation. Only the lower high-field-side corner is characterized, distinguishing this coefficient from upper-inner and lower-outer squareness and from an unqualified inner-squareness quantity. Unlike lower-inner squareness of the plasma boundary, it describes the radially indexed nested flux surfaces rather than exclusively the boundary.
draft.name: lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface

draft.documentation: The source identifies the electrical resistivity of one mobile plasma-facing component unit, rather than plasma-facing components generally, limiter tiles, or wall material. The supplied naming vocabulary has plasma_facing_component but no token for the mobile-unit distinction required by the adjudication. A compliant identifying name therefore requires a vocabulary extension.

draft.description: Major-radius coordinate R of a magnetic flux surface at its inboard, high-field-side midplane intersection, expressed in m. It is the perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame. Under the supplied inboard-midplane convention, this is the minimum major radius on the specified flux surface, on the side inward of the magnetic axis.
draft.documentation: This quantity gives one inboard-midplane position for each magnetic flux surface in an equilibrium profile indexed by poloidal flux. It specializes radial_coordinate by fixing the evaluation locus to the high-field-side midplane, rather than the outboard, low-field-side midplane used by radial_coordinate_at_outboard_midplane. It locates the flux surface rather than the magnetic axis itself, and measures distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, not displacement from the magnetic axis. It is a local coordinate value, not a flux-surface average.
draft.name: radial_coordinate_at_inboard_midplane

draft.description: Local scalar equilibrium metric coefficient G = |∇ρ_tor|^2/R^2, obtained pointwise by dividing the squared Euclidean norm of the spatial gradient of the length-valued toroidal-flux coordinate ρ_tor by the squared major radius R. The coordinate retains its prescribed scale, without boundary normalization or substitution of an arbitrary flux label. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, R is the distance from the toroidal symmetry axis. No spatial averaging is applied. The unit is m^-2.
draft.documentation: This coefficient describes local flux-surface spacing with inverse-square major-radius weighting. Unlike square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude, it includes division by R squared; unlike inverse squared major radius alone, it retains the squared gradient factor. Its denominator is squared major radius, not squared magnetic-field magnitude as in ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude. The related flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius averages the complete local ratio over a closed magnetic flux surface, rather than dividing separately averaged numerator and denominator.
draft.name: ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_major_radius

draft.documentation: The described quantity is already covered by motional_stark_polarization_angle_at_constraint_position: the linear-polarization orientation of motional Stark emission at a constraint position for the specified viewing geometry. The case supplies no physical distinction from that neighbour, and no bound source establishes a different quantity. A separate standard-name record would duplicate the existing quantity.

draft.description: Geometric radial derivative dV/dψ of the cumulative volume V enclosed by a magnetic flux surface with respect to its signed poloidal magnetic-flux coordinate ψ, at a fixed equilibrium time slice with other independent coordinates held fixed. It is obtained by differentiating the enclosed-volume profile V(ψ), and is positive when enclosed volume increases with increasing signed ψ. Its unit is Wb^-1.m^3.
draft.documentation: For each nested closed equilibrium flux surface, V(ψ) is the cumulative volume enclosed from the magnetic axis to that surface. This quantity describes the change in that enclosed volume per change in poloidal magnetic flux, rather than a shell volume, a local volume density, or a derivative of poloidal cross-sectional area. The differentiation coordinate is poloidal magnetic flux, not the toroidal-flux coordinate used by the neighbouring volume-derivative quantity. Integrating dV/dψ between two poloidal-flux values gives the difference in the corresponding enclosed volumes; no population weighting or flux-surface averaging is applied.
draft.name: derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate

draft.description: Signed vertical coordinate Z of the position at which a measurement used to constrain equilibrium reconstruction is given, expressed in m. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, Z = x·ẑ, where x is the position vector from the coordinate origin and ẑ points upward parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis; positive Z denotes height above the zero-height plane.
draft.documentation: This quantity gives the height of an individual constraint position, including positions associated with parallel-current-density, toroidal-current-density, or total-pressure constraints in equilibrium reconstruction. It is specifically the vertical coordinate of the constraint location, rather than that of a generic measurement position or another geometric object. It is a point coordinate, not the constrained observable, a spatial average of height, a magnetic flux, or a normalized flux-surface label. Any flux-surface averaging used to define a current-density constraint applies to that observable, not to this coordinate.
draft.name: vertical_coordinate_of_constraint_position

draft.description: Perimeter of the closed contour formed by one magnetic flux surface in a poloidal plane at fixed toroidal angle, obtained by integrating ds = sqrt(dR² + dZ²) once around the complete contour in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height. The quantity is expressed in m, with no averaging or summation over surfaces.
draft.documentation: This non-negative scalar measures the absolute geometric length of a complete poloidal contour of a selected magnetic flux surface, whose points share a magnetic-flux label. It is positive for a non-degenerate closed contour and excludes local arc segments. Unlike [poloidal-plane cross-sectional area of a flux surface](name:poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface), it measures the contour rather than its enclosed interior; unlike [field-line length](name:field_line_length), it follows a fixed-toroidal-angle cross-section rather than a magnetic field line. It is neither a toroidal circumference nor a radial or vertical span, and the selected surface need not be the last closed flux surface.
draft.name: poloidal_length_of_flux_surface

draft.description: Signed vertical position of the plasma-current centroid in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured in m and positive toward +Z from the coordinate origin. It is obtained as Z_c = ∫_A Z j_tor dS / I_p, where A is the poloidal plasma cross-section, j_tor is the signed toroidal current density, and I_p = ∫_A j_tor dS is the total plasma current.
draft.documentation: This scalar gives the height of the plasma-current center by normalizing the vertical first moment of toroidal current density over the poloidal cross-section by the total plasma current. The weighting uses signed current density, not its absolute value. The vertical direction is parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. This quantity is the centroid's vertical coordinate rather than its major-radius coordinate or its vertical velocity, and the current-weighted centroid need not coincide with the magnetic axis or geometric axis.
draft.name: vertical_coordinate_of_current_center

draft.description: Signed toroidal component of the total equilibrium magnetic field evaluated locally at the magnetic axis, including external-coil and plasma-current contributions, as obtained from the equilibrium reconstruction. It is calculated as B_phi,axis = B_axis · e_phi in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame and expressed in T. Positive values point toward increasing toroidal angle phi, counterclockwise when viewed from above. This is a local component, not a field magnitude, vacuum reference field, or flux-surface average.
draft.documentation: The quantity specifies the toroidal magnetic field at the magnetic axis rather than at an arbitrary point on a flux surface or at a reference major radius. The magnetic axis is the closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged; in an axisymmetric poloidal cross-section it is the interior O-point where the poloidal magnetic field vanishes. The component B_phi is the projection of the reconstructed total equilibrium field onto the unit vector in the direction of increasing phi, with phi = atan2(y, x) in the right-handed cylindrical frame. Both external-coil and plasma-current contributions are retained, unlike a vacuum-field component, which excludes plasma-current contributions. No spatial averaging or magnitude reduction is applied.
draft.name: toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis

draft.description: Safety factor at the magnetic axis, q0, is the dimensionless signed number of toroidal field-line turns per complete poloidal circuit in the limit as nested closed magnetic flux surfaces approach the axis. It is obtained as q0 = lim(rho→0) q(rho), where rho labels the surfaces and vanishes at the axis, and q = (1/(2π)) ∮ (B·∇phi)/(B·∇theta) dtheta over one complete poloidal circuit in axisymmetry or straight-field-line flux coordinates. Here B is the magnetic field, theta is the poloidal angle, and phi is the toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above. The sign is positive when phi increases as theta increases along a field line. The unit is 1.
draft.documentation: The magnetic axis is the closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged; in an axisymmetric poloidal cross-section it is the O-point where the poloidal magnetic field vanishes. The axis safety factor is therefore defined through the neighboring-surface limit rather than by evaluating a poloidal-angle integral directly on the axis. It is a locus-specific value, not a spatial average, and differs from safety factors at the pedestal, internal transport barrier, or plasma boundary by its location. It is not the minimum safety factor over the equilibrium domain, since that minimum need not occur at the axis, nor is it magnetic shear, which describes radial variation of the safety factor.
draft.name: safety_factor_at_magnetic_axis

draft.documentation: The source supplies the vertical Z coordinate, in m, of each point on the plasma-boundary outline used by fixed-boundary codes, typically chosen at psi_norm = 99.x% of the separatrix. The supplied registry instead requires plasma_boundary to mean the last closed magnetic flux surface. These loci are not necessarily identical, so applying the registered name would impose a boundary identification not supported by the source. The registry meaning or source-to-locus mapping must be resolved before a record can be produced.
draft.name: vertical_outline_of_plasma_boundary
